author: product-requirements-expert
title: Filter the veterinarian directory by specialty
summary: Narrow the veterinarian directory to only vets holding a named specialty, on both the HTML page and the machine-readable list. The specialty is carried in the request address; matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive. This slice adds no on-screen control.
acceptance_criteria: Narrowing the HTML directory to a specialty some vets hold lists only those vets, a page at a time.
Narrowing the machine-readable list to a specialty returns only the vets holding it.
A specialty name differing from a stored specialty only by letter case matches (case-insensitive).
A specialty name that only partly matches a stored specialty does not match; the whole name is required.
A specialty name no vet holds returns a normal, empty directory with a success response on both surfaces.
A blank or whitespace-only specialty is treated as no narrowing, exactly as an empty owner search is.
With no specialty named, both surfaces behave exactly as before this requirement.
A narrowed directory spanning more than one page keeps the narrowing in force when moving between pages.
No dropdown, form, or on-screen control is added by this slice.
non_goals: A visible filter control (dropdown/form) — deferred to a separate requirement.
Narrowing to more than one specialty at once.
notes: Narrows NG-9. Reinstates the machine-readable /vets list as a supported surface under this fresh id; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. Empty/whitespace handling mirrors the empty owner-search pattern (REQ-OWN-002). Open questions recorded in docs/prd.md: visible control, multi-specialty narrowing.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Extends the established owner-search filter+pagination pattern to the vet feature; no new module, pattern class, dependency, or ADR. VetController already carries the pagination scaffold (findPaginated/addPaginationModel, VetController.java:50-63); this slice threads an optional whole-name, case-insensitive specialty filter through both existing routes, mirroring OwnerController.processFindForm's empty->broadest normalization (OwnerController.java:94-122) and OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith's derived paged query (OwnerRepository.java:45). VetRepository gains two derived query methods (paged for /vets.html, collection for /vets). The one deliberate adjustment vs the owner pattern: use the Spring Data IgnoreCase derived-query keyword rather than relying on vendor column collation, which generates upper(name)=upper(?) at the query layer and matches cross-vendor -- deliberately sidestepping the PostgreSQL case-sensitivity defect recorded for owner last-name search (system-design Known Defects). Read-confirmed against VetController/VetRepository/Vet/OwnerController/OwnerRepository; IDE semantic oracle not connected this run.
integration_points: /vets.html gains an optional specialty @RequestParam(required=false); when blank/whitespace it strips to absent and the existing findAll(pageable) path runs unchanged, otherwise the filtered paged query runs and its Page drives totalPages/totalElements.
/vets (JSON) gains the same optional specialty param; blank/absent returns the full Vets wrapper as today, non-blank returns only matching vets wrapped in Vets.
vetList.html must expose the active specialty in the model and append it to every pagination link (page/first/prev/next/last) so navigation keeps the filter in force; add specialty only when present.

patterns.description: empty/whitespace param -> broadest search normalization (strip, treat blank as absent) to mirror for the specialty param
Spring Data derived paged query method returning Page<T>; the vet equivalent is findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) plus a non-paged Collection<Vet> overload for the JSON route
existing pagination scaffold (page-1 offset, pageSize 5); the filtered path reuses it, swapping findAll for the filter query

risks.risk: The two new filter query methods could follow the existing @Cacheable("vets") reads (VetRepository.java:44-56); parameterized keys keep filtered results distinct per specialty. There is no vet write path, so cache staleness is not a new concern (Open Question #5).
risks.mitigation: Reuse @Cacheable("vets") for consistency, or omit it on the filter methods -- either is correct; do not add eviction, which the slice does not need.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is @ManyToMany(fetch=EAGER); a paginated query that join-fetches the collection can trigger Hibernate in-memory pagination (HHH000104).
risks.mitigation: This is the identical shape the existing findAll(Pageable) already runs in production, so it introduces no new risk; keep the derived filter query and let Spring Data issue its count+select as it does today. No Distinct is needed -- equality on unique specialty names yields one row per vet.

risks.risk: system-design Known Defects lists the /vets route as 'serves no requirement, pending removal', and the Contracts Implements column does not wire REQ-VET-003 into VetController/VetRepository. This slice reinstates /vets as a supported surface, making that defect row and those Implements cells stale.
risks.mitigation: Doc-sync (post-implementation) retires the Known Defects row and wires REQ-VET-003 into the VetController and VetRepository Implements cells. Not a code concern; flagged so the doc update is not missed. The reinstatement is an already-settled product decision (prd-entry notes), so this is not a design conflict.

notes: Verdict minor: established pattern, small adjustment; no docs/system-design.md or ADR edit needed at design time (the doc changes above are post-implementation doc-sync, keeping the state-vs-code discipline). Whole-name equality (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, not StartingWith) satisfies the prefix-rejection acceptance criterion. No design-doc-autofix records to audit. Next agent: feature-implementer.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Specialty flows into a Spring Data derived query (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase) bound as a JPA parameter (upper(name)=upper(?)); no string concatenation, no SQL/JPQL injection surface.

Specialty is emitted only into pagination URLs via Thymeleaf @{/vets.html(...,specialty=${specialty})} link expressions, which URL-encode query-parameter values and auto-escape the href attribute context; specialty is never rendered as raw HTML text, so no reflected XSS.
normalizeSpecialty strips input and treats blank/whitespace as absent, mirroring the owner-search pattern; untrusted request input is handled safely with no unsafe sinks.
No auth/authz change: the vet directory and machine-readable list remain the same public read-only surface as before; no secrets, deserialization, or path/command sinks introduced.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: normalizeSpecialty helper extracted to a named private method and called from both routes — no logic duplication, Javadoc is accurate and complete
VetRepository new methods carry correct Spring Data derived-query names (IgnoreCase suffix), matching Javadoc, and the same @Transactional/@Cacheable annotations as the existing findAll siblings
findPaginated branches on null specialty cleanly with an early return; single responsibility preserved
vetList.html threads specialty=${specialty} through every pagination link; Thymeleaf null-param-dropping correctly handles the no-filter case without additional template branching

normalizeSpecialty null-to-null and whitespace-to-null normalization mirrors the intent of OwnerController processFindForm (grep-confirmed, IDE oracle not connected); deviation from inline to extracted helper is justified by dual call sites
No prohibited naming suffixes, no abbreviations, no type-name repetition in method names

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: All 8 new test method names were copied verbatim from the prd-entry test_names field (e.g., specialtyNarrowingIsCaseInsensitive, blankSpecialtyIsTreatedAsAbsent), but testing-principles.md § Test Naming requires the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward. The PRD-specified names are behavior-descriptive noun phrases rather than subject-outcome pairs. Either the PRD test_names should be updated to follow the convention, or an explicit exception for PRD-mandated test names should be added to the testing brief. The feature-implementer correctly followed what the PRD specified; resolution belongs with the PRD author.

Three tests (unknownSpecialtyReturnsEmptyDirectoryWithOkStatus, blankSpecialtyIsTreatedAsAbsent, noSpecialtyParamPreservesExistingBehavior) each make two separate mockMvc.perform() calls exercising the HTML and JSON surfaces independently. testing-principles.md § Tests Are Specifications says one logical assertion per test. The prd-entry mapped a single test_name to each acceptance criterion that explicitly covers both surfaces, creating structural pressure to combine two distinct HTTP interactions in one method. A failure in such a test does not immediately indicate which surface is broken. The appropriate fix — splitting each dual-surface test into two surface-specific methods — requires the PRD to accept two test_names per criterion, which is a PRD-granularity decision.

approved_aspects: All 8 PRD-specified test_names are present and match exactly
Both HTTP surfaces (HTML and JSON) are covered for all applicable behaviors
Case-insensitive matching and whole-name-not-prefix behaviors tested against real H2 via ClinicServiceTests @DataJpaTest
Factory methods james() and helen() wrap Vet construction, meeting the testing brief factory-method requirement
AssertJ fluent assertions used in ClinicServiceTests; Spring MVC result matchers appropriate for controller tests
No new mock infrastructure introduced — the 6 new controller tests rely on the existing @MockitoBean VetRepository that the brief classifies as tolerated pre-existing usage
All 8 new tests pass with 0 failures and 0 skips; build green
